Reaching x=9 requires exactly 9 R moves because R is the only move that increases x; reaching y=9 requires exactly 9 D moves because D is the only move that increases y. Every sequence of 9 R moves and 9 D moves is monotone, ends at (9,9), and stays within nonnegative coordinates. Conversely, any monotone path determines its ordered move sequence. This correspondence is bijective: the move sequence reconstructs the successive coordinates, and each valid coordinate path gives one move sequence. Thus paths are represented exactly by length-18 strings over {R,D} with exactly nine R and exactly nine D. The convention D<R orders these strings lexicographically: compare at the first position where two strings differ, and the string with D at that position is smaller. The later constraints restrict this universe; step 1 only fixes the representation and comparison order.
